How Syrona groups concepts into chapters, as shown in the dashboard. A reference: none of this is needed to run Syrona. Everything comes from the vocabulary tables of your CDM (`concept`, `concept_ancestor`, `concept_relationship`).

## Conditions

Standard SNOMED concepts are counted. Each condition gets three groupings (`chapter_type` in `condition_chapters`):

| Grouping | How |
|---|---|
| `body_system` | the SNOMED hierarchy under *Disorder of body system* (concept 4180628) |
| `disease_category` | the SNOMED hierarchy under *Disease* (4274025), without the body-system branch |
| `icd10_chapter` | the ICD-10 code the condition is mapped from (`Mapped from` to ICD10 or ICD10CM): its first three characters give the ICD-10 chapter, I to XXII. Without a mapping: `(Unmapped)` |

The SNOMED groupings have two levels: the direct children of the anchor concept, and their children. A condition can be in several chapters, because SNOMED concepts can have several parents.

Attributes (`condition_attributes`) are SNOMED relationships: finding site, associated morphology, clinical course, causative agent, occurrence and pathology.

## Procedures

Standard concepts of any vocabulary are counted. Two groupings, each with two levels:

| Grouping | How |
|---|---|
| `by_method` | the SNOMED hierarchy under *Procedure by method* (4029205) |
| `by_site` | the SNOMED hierarchy under *Procedure by site* (4180627) |

Attributes are the direct procedure site and the method.

## Drugs

Every drug record is rolled up to its ingredients (standard `Ingredient` concepts of RxNorm or RxNorm Extension, through `concept_ancestor`), so a combination product counts for each of its ingredients. Each ingredient gets its ATC 1st level group, the 14 anatomical main groups (for example *Cardiovascular system*). Without an ATC link: `(Unmapped)`. Drugs have no attributes.

## What the vocabulary must contain

The vocabularies SNOMED, RxNorm, ATC and ICD10, as downloaded from [Athena](https://athena.ohdsi.org). Without ICD10, every condition is `(Unmapped)` in the ICD-10 chapters; without ATC, every drug is `(Unmapped)`.
